GS Delta-One head, Rich Privorotsky, on latest in AI:

Four stories to unpack:
First, CXMT is a legitimate concern for memory economics. 
Second, Microsoft’s Maia 300 custom chips, moving to TSMC’s 2nm process.Incrementally negative for merchant GPU suppliers (NVDA), positive for the custom silicon supply chain and aggregate compute consumption. 
Third, Hock Tan’s comments comparing AI investors to gamblers have been taken wildly out of context. Both Broadcomand Intel reaffirmed exceptionally strong demand for another 2–3 years, potentially through 2030. Tan sees compute demand exceeding supply and explicitly acknowledged that frontier labs generating substantial revenue can afford expensive financing. LT ROI is a legitimate question, but hardly a revelation.  
Fourth, Meta’s Muse Wonder and Wonder Full look genuinely competitive at the frontier,potentially adding another serious player alongside OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Some questions around benchmarking, but impressive nonetheless. Prediction markets also anticipating another major Google release imminently. 

What do I make of all this? Competition fuels competition, and competition requires more compute. The frontier keeps advancing, driven by Western closed source labs trying to outdo one another. Hardly bearish for aggregate compute demand, even if the economics shift around the supply chain. Think the legitimate concerns are around the ability to complete capacity/deliver power relative to expectations and that is fueling further de-rating in the capex vertical.

We are witnessing a historic shift.

The annual spread between the S&P 500's earnings yield and the 10Y Note yield is down to -1.5 percentage points, its lowest since 2009.

Since 2022, this yield difference has fallen -440 basis points, its largest 5-year decline since the 1970s.

As a result, the S&P 500's equity risk premium is on track to post its 3rd consecutive negative annual reading, the longest streak since 2002.

This suggests that, on a yield basis, theoretically less risky 10Y Treasuries are now more attractive than the S&P 500.

In other words, investors are receiving a higher yield from Treasuries than from the S&P 500, despite the additional risk of owning stocks.

Historically, a negative equity risk premium has been associated with strong risk appetite and stretched equity valuations.

We expect an eventful Q4 ahead.

The rise of digital assets has been driven via anti-fragility.

Frontier Math breakthroughs and quantum computing are perceived to be an existential threat. These threats do have merit. But I am confident we will navigate them at large and there will be no disastrous event. 

The concept of anti-fragility means something benefits from volatility and is not crushed by it. Over time the system becomes stronger. I view any future changes to the cryptography underpinning public blockchains as this. 

If I were to identify the most fragile point for blockchains it's not the underlying cryptography. Its the fact malicious state changes are irreversible and are physic like events. You cannot reverse time after a collision has occurred. Finality is the collision. 

I am fully pro having some form of policy engine imbedded directly at the block builder/sequencer level where malicious transactions cannot be mined. This to me remains a far significant threat vector than frontier math AI breakthroughs.

$NVDA CES 2025 projections and Elon's prediction on $TSLA + 1 Billion humanoids in the next decade, seems to be speeding up.

But going from 2-3 years (potentially to a decade), and compressing that down to 1 or 2 years (to achieve 80%+ of tasks in unfamiliar environemnts) is a significant change in outlook.

When I first got into crypto from a technical perspective there were many incredibly interesting esoteric ideas that were truly frontier ideas.

I remember pre 2020 prediction markets were first called truth markets. But on-chain infrastructure had not caught up yet to make the idea go mainstream.

It seems we are entering a phase now where these esoteric ideas may become front and centre. Few ideas being the following:

[1] Proof of Humanity: This to me now seems tautological and digital interactions seek trust now more than ever. Adversarial actors and AI passing the Turing test for both audio/visual interactions seems sufficient enough to have a PoH everywhere (emails, online calls, socials).

[2] PQ Cryptography: Emerging threat vectors from Quantum computing and breakthroughs in frontier Math that may expose weaknesses in traditional ECDSA. The ability to attain a private key from an exposed public key. Explains the rise of ZEC as a hedge to threat vectors to Bitcoin core and it's ossification leading to a delayed response.

[3] Private Inference: Concerns arising from frontier labs distilling their own users. Corporations are seeking hosting their own models ands training them on their own operations. Coinbase recently announced they trained their own model for a specific business function. I do think private inference of frontier intelligence protecting user thought and intellectual property will have a strong attractor over time.

These ideas were early and have existed for some time but the world they were building for did not exist. It's difficult to see where we are going and the end state but I now think these ideas will begin to see wider adoption.

there‘s been a lot of rumors and speculation around it, but this recent livestream by @TuomHolmberg and @chrisakvn essentially says it all. so let me break it down for you:

one of the fastest growing trends in commerce right now is live shopping. Pioneered by Whatnot, and now followed by essentially every big platform: TikTok Shop, eBay Live, you name it.

think of Ripmart as the first truly onchain native version of something like Whatnot, powered by Collector Crypt's infrastructure.

why is this so exciting? a few reasons.

the UX.

as a collector, you don't rip packs on a livestream just because it's fun. you do it chasing that one grail you've always wanted. most of the time you don't hit it, that's part of the game, and you end up at home with a pile of worthless cards you never wanted and spent way too much money on.

with Collector Crypt underneath, Ripmart changes that. instant liquidity through buyback offers, just like you know from the gacha. you can immediately sell back, preserve your liquidity, and get way more runway to keep chasing the grail you actually want, while no more pile of worthless cards at home.

sounds simple, but that one feature gives collectors a 10x better experience (and likely also success rate in finding their grail). which makes choosing Ripmart over Whatnot and the rest a no brainer going forward.

then there is the onchain adoption.

the onchain part is obviously fully abstracted away. it just feels like using a slick new livestreaming and social app.

but what that means for @solana and @Collector_Crypt is massive. this is one of those rare events that could onboard hundreds of thousands, maybe millions of users onchain without them even realizing it, driven purely by their love for collectibles and a genuinely great shopping experience.

the supply of tokenized collectibles on Solana is about to explode. it brings a ton of liquidity to Collector's marketplace, better discovery, and adds an entirely new, highly sought after asset class on top: ungraded cards.

the traction this brings to CC and Solana is going to be huge. and the best part: it's fully organic and therefore sustainable, driven by an asset class people genuinely love and an experience orders of magnitude better than anything out there today.

and of course, Tuom wouldn't be Tuom if there wasn't a lot more going on behind the scenes, stuff beyond most people's imagination, that'll make sure Ripmart isn't just a nice idea but gets the adoption it deserves from day one.

but more on that later, once the time is right.

until then: Tuom mode.

The fundamental investment era for crypto

It might be the topic du jour, but I’ve been writing at @RealVision all year that matket forces were correcting years of misalignment and distortion. 

For four years after I entered this space, what vexed me most was how unstable traditional equity-like factors were when applied to this asset class. I wanted to understand what actually drove token value. Quality had to be part of the answer, from first principles, but there weren’t enough protocols with product-market fit, disciplined supply and incentives aligned between insiders and token holders to make the case convincing.

The last cycle left investors disillusioned: too much VC-era grift, dilution and protocol teams whose incentives had little to do with their token holders. Trump’s arrival changed the regulatory environment, while market pressure from pissed off investors and evangelists began to exert pressure. We now have a situation where a protocol cannot just have product-market fit. It must compete on tokenomics / value accrual. Distortions haven't disappeared, but they are declining. Market forces and proper regulatory guardrails will see to that.

The top third of my quality basket is up about 35% through September, while Bitcoin and the cap-weighted Top 100 are both down about 8%. From 2022 through 2025, that basket lost about 71% while Bitcoin gained 88%. Nine months prove little statistically. Still, I’m increasingly convinced that protocols without product-market fit, supply discipline and a credible path for value to reach token holders will underperform those that have all three.
